newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat-ordered audit finds Palestinian corruption.
newsitem.headline: Arafat-ordered audit finds Palestinian corruption.

text.p: An auditing office set up by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Saturday the self-rule government in the West Bank and Gaza had misused $326 million in public funds last year.
The 600-page report by the Palestinian Authority's Monitoring Institution was the first official criticism of corruption within the administration since self-rule began in 1994.

"We have estimated the mismanagement and squandering of public funds at around $326 million in one year from December 1995 to December 1996," Monitoring Institution chief Jarrar al-Qudwa told Reuters.
He said the report, a copy of which was handed to Arafat, had not been made public yet.

Qudwa's comments coincided with increasing complaints by Palestinians and their elected representatives in the Palestinian Legislative Council of corruption by cabinet officials and government employees.
Palestinian lawmakers on Wednesday charged that the Palestinian Authority was using taxpayers' money on villas and cars for ministers and other senior officials.
"For example we found that $45-$50 million should have gone to the budget from custom fees on cars, but this money was lost on giving people cars without paying customs," Qudwa said.
He said the Palestinian Authority's losses from mismanaging funds for projects and improper distribution of state land was estimated at $67 million.
He did not say if any of the mismanaged money came from donations from foreign states.
"Our report mentions some officials by name who have given certain companies projects to work on because they have personal interests with those companies," Qudwa told Voice of Palestine radio.
He said his report would be made public soon.
"Any money that is spent without the permission of the Finance Ministry is money squandered," he said.
Finance Minister Mohammad Zuhdi al-Nashashibi acknowledged publicly last week that several companies functioning in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank had not paid taxes.
He also said reform was needed in Palestinian Authority ministries.
